subjects.name: Elizabeth Tyler and Edward Young Clarke

summary: The Ku Klux Klan, from its founding by Confederate veterans in Pulaski, Tennessee, and its Reconstruction-era terror against freed Black people and voters, to its 1920s revival as a mass-membership pyramid scheme.

evidence.note: Six Confederate veterans decide to form the club in the latter half of 1866
Tennessee Democrats ally with the Klan in 1867 and it becomes a paramilitary group
Klan intimidates Black voters and Grant supporters during the 1868 election
Detailed account of Klansmen beating a Black preacher nearly to death
After the 1871 Klan Act prosecutions the first Klan is no longer a force by 1872
Simmons launches the second Klan in 1915, inspired by Birth of a Nation
PR agents Tyler and Clarke take over recruitment for an 80 percent cut
Second Klan structured as a multi-level marketing scheme with paid recruiters
Vigilante violence in Oregon, Oklahoma, Indiana, Kansas and southern Illinois
Stephenson conviction and collapse of membership by the late 1920s

notes: Transcript dates the founding to the latter half of 1866; most histories give December 1865, so covered_span starts 1866 per the transcript. The end year of the decline is garbled in the transcript (read as 1927). Tyler and Clarke grouped as one secondary subject; Hiram Evans also has a segment and is in keywords.
